newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT - Indigo 1997 loss revise.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Indigo 1997 loss revise.

text.p: Lehman Brothers said it expected Israel's Indigo NV to lose $0.81 per share in 1997 against its previous forecast of a $0.94 loss.

Lehman analyst Ted Kundtz said the company's fourth quarter 1996 loss of $0.25 was lower than the $0.30 deficit he had expected. He said a major factor was "higher gross margins, 26.4 percent versus our expectation of 22.0 percent."
While Lehman narrowed the forecasted loss for the year, it widened it for first quarter 1997 to $0.32 from its previous estimate of a $0.29 loss.

Kundtz estimated that Indigo would lose $0.20 per share in the second quarter of 1997 versus his previous forecast of a $0.26 deficit, in Q3 the deficit would be $0.17 versus the original estimate of minus $0.22 and in the fourth quarter the loss would be $0.12 versus an earlier forecast of minus $0.17.
"Product revenues were up 10 percent year over year and eight percent sequentially. The company demonstrated good expense control in the quarter," Kundtz said.
It maintained its 3-Neutral rating for the maker of digital printing systems.
